facts.text: The launch file names the franka_gripper_node process franka_gripper and loads config/franka_gripper_node.yaml through rosparam.
The example node config sets publish_rate 30 Hz, default_speed 0.1 m/s and default_grasp_epsilon inner/outer 0.005 m; they are configurable ROS parameters, not device bounds.
The node constructs SimpleActionServer<StopAction> on the relative name "stop".
The node constructs SimpleActionServer<GraspAction> on the relative name "grasp".
The node constructs SimpleActionServer<MoveAction> on the relative name "move".
The node constructs SimpleActionServer<HomingAction> on the relative name "homing".
The stop handler calls gripper.stop() and the homing handler calls gripper.homing().
The move handler calls gripper.move(goal->width, goal->speed).
The grasp handler calls gripper.grasp(goal->width, goal->speed, goal->force, goal->epsilon.inner, goal->epsilon.outer).
The node publishes sensor_msgs/JointState on the relative name "joint_states".
The node fills each of the two finger positions from gripper_state.width * 0.5, so each value is half of the total opening width.
The node obtains robot_ip, default_speed and default_grasp_epsilon from ROS parameters.
The node obtains publish_rate, joint_names and stop_at_shutdown from ROS parameters.
The gripper documentation says StopAction aborts a running action and can be used to stop applying forces after grasping.
The gripper documentation says GraspAction succeeds when the finger distance is within the inner and outer epsilon around the requested width.
Grasp.action declares width in metres, speed in metres per second and force in newtons, and returns success and error.
Move.action declares width in metres and speed in metres per second, and returns success and error.
Stop.action declares no goal fields and returns success and error.
The franka_gazebo plugin advertises the relative "franka_control/set_user_stop" std_srvs/SetBool service to simulate the user stop.
The franka_gazebo documentation calls set_user_stop a special service only available in franka_gazebo for simulating the user stop; it is not a hardware stop service.

safe_state.description: The fixed StopAction acknowledges the native gripper.stop() result. Older pending goals must settle before a fresh stop can confirm safety. This is a software native stop, not a physical e-stop; stopping grasp force may release a load.
